newsitem.title: USA: Elder-Beerman files suit vs Carson, Pirie.
newsitem.headline: Elder-Beerman files suit vs Carson, Pirie.

text.p: The private Elder-Beerman Stores Corp said Tuesday it filed suit against Carson Pirie Scott & Co, charging Carson broke a confidentiality agreement.

The October 3 1995 agreement prohibited Carson from trying to buy or control the department store, which is reorganizing under Chapter 11, for a period of two years after it was signed, Elder-Beerman's legal counsel Richard Chesley said.

A company statement said the lawsuit was triggered by Carson's "recent public announcements -believed to be tied to its misappropiation of confidential Elder-Beerman business information- about its interest in acquiring Elder-Beerman."
Chesley said the "public announcement was an article in the Milwaukee newspapers on 5 June but declined to elaborate on the "misappropriation of confidential business information."
Elder-Beerman said the suit, which seeks injunctive relief from the court, also claims Carson sought to acquire the company through its own actions and in concert with others.
Carson spokesmen were not immediately available for comment.

Elder-Beerman said the company entered the confidentiality agreements when it was in merger discussions with Carson before it filed for bankruptcy on October 17 1995. The company filed the suit with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Dayton, Ohio.
